mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction date is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) predict negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as weak labor market and weak demand jointly depress growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakness coupled with demand softening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when the interaction pattern occurs (IC > 0.05) or unemployment claims fall while demand rises in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above its prior month's level coincides with a positive S&P 5-day forward return as it signals accelerating output momentum that is discounted less heavily in the near term.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during INDPRO > +2% months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate lower future rate hikes and improved equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for fewer than three months in the window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in a quarter, it triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as market anticipates a potential rate hike pause and stronger growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% in the current quarter
regime_hint: labor market tightening approaching low-rate floor
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE crosses below 4.5% (or fails to do so within the quarter).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (HOUST) above their prior month's levels predicts a negative S&P 50-day forward return due to over-heating labor and demand dynamics that may prompt rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and HOUST increases in the same month
regime_hint: labor and demand expansion beyond sustainable levels
failure_condition: 50-day forward returns are positive when both proxies rise together (IC > 0.05) or either proxy falls in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 400 billion dollars for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it indicates weakening industrial capacity and potential supply constraints.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the two-month RSAFS decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-week moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher discounting of future equity cash flows amid aggressive policy tightening.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when the 12-week MA of FEDFUNDS is above 5% (or the threshold is not crossed in the window).
